title: Interview questions
note: The interviewer asked these questions in every session, and asked the per-tool questions once for each builder.

questions.text: How complete does your current resume feel to you right now?
When you picture a resume you'd feel good (confident) sending, what matters most to you?
Do you feel this template is modern or better than what you get in Word, why?
What do you think about the amount of freedom/flexibility this tool gives you when creating your resume? Do you feel constrained by the tool, or can you create a resume that's truly yours?
What do you like about the experience (e.g., drag-and-drop, step-by-step instructional flow)? Why?
Does this tool do a good job validating that your resume is strong while you work on it?
Does it struggle to present your experience cleanly on one page? If so, which one and how?
Which of these two builders have a template design experience that stands out, and which one feels more generic according to you? Are there any significant differences?
Do you feel this template is modern or better than what you get in Word, compared to the other one, and vice versa? Which one would you choose to help you stand out in a pile of candidates?
What is the difference between the amount of freedom each tool gives to you when creating your resume? Do you feel constrained by the tool, or can you create a resume that's truly yours?
Do you prefer the drag-and-drop experience freedom of one tool, or the more step-by-step instructional flow of the other? Why?
Did either tool make you rethink how you tell your professional story? Which one?
Which tool does a better job validating that your resume is strong while you work on it?
Do you feel either tool struggles to present your experience cleanly on one page? If so, which one and how?
If you were applying to two different roles, which tool would you trust more to tailor your resume and create multiple strong versions?

I understand the resume may not be complete, and you would need a bit more time, but after spending 1 hour more with each of these resume builders, which one would produce a resume that is more likely to give you confidence and impress recruiters?
Which tool better matches where you are in your career right now?
Who do you think should not use each of these tools?
Anything else to add that you would like, that you think we should know?
Would you be willing to pay for access to either of these platforms or both?
